title: By two years, most children use one hand while the other holds on
summary: The CDC says that by two years, most children hold something in one hand while the other hand works, such as taking a lid off.
body: The CDC's two-year cognitive list includes holding something in one hand while using the other hand. The printed example is holding a container and taking the lid off. The item is a two-handed action on the US list of what most children do by age two. It does not explain how a lid seals, and it is not a warning about what belongs in a container.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Years
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the cognitive item about holding something in one hand while the other takes a lid off.
